// Edited fictional examples from the J/K/R research bundles, not live model output.
export const sources = {
  J1: {id: 'J1', kind: 'quote', en: 'Before deciding, please show the alternatives and what we give up.', ko: '결정하기 전에 선택지와 각 선택에서 포기할 점을 보여 달라고 했어요.'},
  J2: {id: 'J2', kind: 'quote', en: 'Just tell me whether it passed.', ko: '테스트가 통과했는지만 알려 달라고 했어요.'},
  J3: {id: 'J3', kind: 'quote', en: 'I need the failure cases and a way back before approving.', ko: '위험한 시스템 변경을 승인하기 전에, 실패할 수 있는 경우와 되돌릴 방법을 요청했어요.'},
  J4: {id: 'J4', kind: 'summary', en: 'The assistant ignored a requested rollback plan. The user repeated the requirement and added a long explanation.', ko: 'AI가 요청받은 복구 계획을 다루지 않았어요. 사용자는 같은 조건을 다시 말하며 길게 설명했어요.'},
  J5: {id: 'J5', kind: 'quote', en: "I don't always want short answers. I want enough to judge what to do.", ko: '늘 짧은 답을 원하는 것은 아니며, 무엇을 할지 판단할 만큼 설명해 주길 바란다고 말했어요.'},
  K1: {id: 'K1', kind: 'summary', en: 'The user invited five ideas and a playful tone.', ko: '사용자는 아이디어 다섯 가지와 장난기 있는 말투를 요청했어요.'},
  K2: {id: 'K2', kind: 'quote', en: 'Now keep to this scope until it works.', ko: '아이디어 하나를 고른 사용자는 작동할 때까지 그 범위를 지켜 달라고 했어요.'},
  K3: {id: 'K3', kind: 'quote', en: 'Thanks. That makes the next step clearer.', ko: '문제를 고친 뒤, 다음 단계가 더 분명해졌다며 감사를 전했어요.'},
  K4: {id: 'K4', kind: 'quote', en: 'Please follow the two conditions I already gave you.', ko: 'AI가 조건 하나를 빠뜨리자, 사용자는 이미 말한 두 조건을 따라 달라고 요청했어요.'},
  R1: {id: 'R1', kind: 'quote', originalLanguage: 'ko', ko: '이 답변은 회의에서 읽을 거예요. 배경과 예시를 충분히 넣어 주세요.', en: 'I will read this answer at a meeting. Please include plenty of background and examples.'},
  R2: {id: 'R2', kind: 'quote', originalLanguage: 'ko', ko: '휴대폰 알림으로 볼 요약은 핵심 한 문장만 보내 주세요.', en: 'For the summary I will see as a phone notification, please send just one sentence with the key point.'},
  R3: {id: 'R3', kind: 'quote', originalLanguage: 'ko', ko: "동료가 '너는 늘 말을 길게 해'라고 했는데, 그건 동료의 평가예요. 제 말 길이를 잰 기록은 없어요.", en: "A colleague said, 'You always talk at length,' but that is their assessment. There is no record measuring how long I speak."},
};

source.avatar/README.md:
# Avatar

Avatar is a local CLI and host skill for reviewing explicitly recorded choices and
user-confirmed personal criteria. It keeps quoted reasons, provenance, versions, revocations, and
read-only Distill history projections in SQLite.

Avatar does not collect conversations automatically, infer personality, authenticate speakers, or
promote project exceptions into personal criteria. It works without Stage or Distill.

## Requirements

- Python 3.9 or newer
- No third-party packages

The default database is `~/.avatar/avatar.db`. Override it with `--home <directory>` or the
`AVATAR_HOME` environment variable. The database stays outside the plugin installation cache.

## Commands

Run commands from this repository with `python3 avatar/scripts/avatar.py`. From an installed host
plugin, resolve `scripts/avatar.py` from the plugin root.

```text
avatar choice add --idempotency-key <key> --payload-file <json>
avatar criterion propose --idempotency-key <key> --payload-file <json>
avatar criterion confirm <PC-id> --version <N> --idempotency-key <key> --payload-file <json>
avatar criterion revise <PC-id> --idempotency-key <key> --payload-file <json>
avatar criterion revoke <PC-id> --idempotency-key <key> --payload-file <json>
avatar source attach --idempotency-key <key> --file <distill-history.json>
avatar show [--choice <CH-id> | --criterion <PC-id>] [--json]
avatar export
avatar check --refs <avatar-ref,...>
```

All mutating commands require an idempotency key. Replaying the same request returns the original
result with `replayed: true`. Reusing the key for different content returns
`E_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` and writes nothing.

Confirmation creates a new immutable version and returns its ref. For example, confirming
proposal `@1` returns confirmed version `@2`. Use the returned ref. Revision creates a new
unconfirmed proposal; it does not reuse the earlier user's confirmation as its source.

## Data boundaries

- `CH-` records belong to Avatar and describe one explicit choice.
- `PC-` records belong to Avatar and describe versioned personal criteria.
- Distill `CR-` history is stored as a read-only projection. `show` labels it historical and does
  not claim that it is current.
- `export` emits `criteria-snapshot/1` with `scope: personal`. It includes only the current
  `user_confirmed` versions.
- `check` returns `eligible_current`, `proposed`, `superseded`, `revoked`, `scope_mismatch`, or
  `unknown`. Consumers must apply only `eligible_current` refs.

## Local web preview

Run `python3 avatar/scripts/avatar_web.py` from the repository root, then open
`http://127.0.0.1:4173`. The first screen uses clearly marked fictional records.
Import a file created with `python3 avatar/scripts/avatar.py show --json > avatar-records.json`.
Files are processed in the browser tab. Import alone does not upload them. The preview does not persist imported
records or reflection notes; download the report before closing or refreshing the tab.

To explicitly connect a local store, start the viewer with `--home <avatar-directory>` and click
the local-record button. The server reads that store only after the request. It never writes records.
Without `--home`, local-store access is disabled, including the default `~/.avatar` store.

The preview summarizes linked criteria, differing choices, and wording revisions deterministically.
It does not infer fixed personality traits or validate psychological constructs. Imported
criteria reflect the file's capture time; use the CLI `check` before relying on them for a decision.
Limits: 8 MiB per imported file and 2,000 choices or criteria. External history projections are not
treated as current criteria. Reports include private source text, so review them before sharing.

To enable optional AI reflection, install and sign in to Claude Code CLI, then start with
`python3 avatar/scripts/avatar_web.py --ai claude`. Select 1–60 records in the viewer, inspect the
exact payload, and confirm before sending. Questions, choices, quoted reasons, project names,
conditions, and referenced criterion versions go to Claude using the signed-in account's usage.
Origin paths and unrelated record metadata are excluded. Imported criteria are marked with their
confirmation, current-version, and revocation status; they are not silently adopted.

The CLI runs Sonnet without tools, skills, MCP servers, or saved sessions. Each interpretation cites
supplied choice IDs and includes an alternative explanation. Unknown evidence IDs fail validation.
This checks references, not whether an interpretation is correct. Users can add corrections to the
downloaded report; these notes do not update the underlying criteria. No analysis runs on page load.
AI requests are limited to one at a time and a 90-second timeout. The browser accepts up to 55,000
JavaScript string units in serialized input; the server separately limits its JSON representation
to 60,000 characters. Individual input text fields are limited to 20,000 characters.

Working-style downloads are user-selected experiments. Public articles are attributed and adapted;
they are not the authors' own AI configurations or endorsements. Downloads do not install themselves
or overwrite project instructions. Attach the file to the intended AI conversation and state its scope.

This localhost preview has no accounts, payments, or public deployment. Do not expose this stdlib
development server through a public proxy. The Korean UI is a first product preview.

### Fictional conversation preview

Open `http://127.0.0.1:4173/stories` to read three fictional people in Korean or English.
The records and interpretations are edited examples, not a live conversation-analysis feature.
R's Korean records contrast requested answers for a meeting and a notification, then separate a
colleague's quoted assessment from measured behavior. Original Korean stays visible in English mode,
with the translation labeled separately. J and K retain their original English evidence.
Read three scenes, inspect the source text and context, compare interpretations across scenes,
and edit an interpretation. Reading order does not establish when the conversations occurred.
Edits and unfinished drafts stay in memory, separately for each person and scene. Reloading clears them. The page has
no AI calls, uploads, analytics, or ad scripts. Its entry link opens a new tab to preserve records
already imported in the main viewer. The rest of the viewer remains in Korean.

## Development

Run the package suite from the repository root:

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s avatar/tests -q
python3 -m unittest tests.test_plugin_contracts -q
node --test avatar/tests/*.test.mjs
```
